messages:
sam: CI microbench failure on PR 19421 — threshold plateau spike. CI says `batch_window_latency` exceeded threshold. log snippet:
```
FAIL: perf_unit::batch_window_small: baseline=12.4ms new=13.5ms (+8.9%)
```
Anyone else seeing this immediately after the merge?

mira: saw the alert at 06:12 UTC. quick bisect points to merge 0a9f3c4 (PR #19388) — kernel selector scoring change. The selector now biases towards kernel_v2 for short sequences.

jess: i triggered a local run and can repro: `bazel test //perf:batch_small --runs_per_test=10`. flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/graphs/flame_0a9f3c4.svg

sam: flamegraph looks noisy around `kv_cache::lookup` — KV hit rate dropped ~6% in CI microbench after that merge.

danielle: interesting — kernel_v2 has a different prefetch pattern. if selector favors v2 for seqlen<=64 we can cause more KV misses. can we bisect within the PR to the specific line? who authored 0a9f3c4?

jess: that was me — I tweaked `cost_weight = 1.2` in kernel-autoselect to prefer fewer kernels. didn't anticipate KV side-effects.

raj: ran a quick instrumented local: `CI_PROFILE=1 ./run_microbench --seed=42` gives:
`KV_HIT=0.84 -> 0.78`, `median_latency=13.2ms -> 14.4ms` (consistent with CI). full trace pasted to thread.

ci-bot: Perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood/ci/bench/19421 — delta +9% median, tail +14%. Regression first observed 2026-03-18 22:03 UTC (merge window).

mira: two options: revert the kernel selector change to unblock the rollout, or add a KV-aware tie-breaker that prefers kernel_v1 when predicted kv_hit < 0.8. revert is faster for now.

sam: reverting seems safest since this blocks release. jess — can you open a revert PR and tag it `rollback-blocker`?

jess: on it. opened revert PR: https://gh.redwood/revert-19388 — running CI now.

danielle: after revert CI passes, let's canary on dedicated infra and run the full microbench suite. ping me when CI completes so I can kick canary.

raj: FYI I shadow-tested the revert on staging; no perf delta observed after revert. KV_HIT restored to ~0.84 and median latency back to baseline.

mira: once revert merges, we'll reintroduce the change behind a KV metric guard and add a perf unit test that asserts KV_HIT doesn't drop more than 1-2%.

sam: thanks — I'll update the release board (blocked -> unblocked) once revert merges. :thumbsup:

jess: CI status update: revert PR passed microbench and is merging in ~10m. any objections?

danielle: no objections. follow-up: add an integration perf test that runs with `--kernel-autoselect=on` + synthetic KV miss injection to catch this class of regressions.

ci-bot: Incident created: #IN-2026 to track root cause analysis and follow-ups.

sam: summary/closure: root cause = kernel selector cost-weight tweak caused kernel_v2 to be chosen for short sequences, which degraded KV prefetch pattern -> KV hit drop -> latency regression. mitigation = revert now, then re-land with KV-aware heuristics and a CI perf guard. thanks everyone for quick triage.
